narration: This video uses accepted Chromium screenshots, not live footage.
Everything is synthetic; inference is fake.
TrustFlow asks: was the action authorized, and did it happen once?
The Planner proposes. Deterministic policy decides risk.
Humans approve high-risk actions. Execution preserves operation identity.
Verification reads ledger evidence. Muse inference remains pending.
This synthetic five-thousand-dollar transfer pauses.
The screen shows the plan version, payload and full hash.
Approval authorizes that exact snapshot.
Accepted checks reject missing credentials, wrong hashes and replayed decisions.
The model cannot grant itself permission.
After approval, one transaction commits.
Independent SQLite observations match the authorized operation and conserved total.
A separate concurrent approval test produces one transfer.
A rejected three-thousand-dollar request creates no transfer.
Reload preserves rejection; late approval cannot revive it.
The ledger independently supports the result.
Controlled fault injection holds a real worker past timeout.
After that worker commits, reconciliation finds the original transaction.
An injected fake review failure leaves verification pending.
Verification-only retry completes without another transfer.
Now the backend is killed after SQLite commit, before saving success.
Signal nine interrupts the process. The same container restarts into verification pending.
Verification-only retry preserves the original transaction, approval hash and snapshot.
This demonstrates a controlled checkpoint, not every storage failure.
Missing mandatory policy evidence fails closed before tools run.
This is a local retrieval check, with no ledger mutation.
One command repeats six scenarios and publishes evidence.
Accepted results are fake-mode checks.
Live Muse evaluation remains pending.
